## 1. What was read

**909 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 449 | 132 | 85 | 225 | 18 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -29%, sysbio -25%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 108, Science 100, JAMA 92, Nucleic Acids Res 80, Bioinformatics 56, Lancet 46.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**`cell-therapy` gains three cards and each one leaves the CD19 template in a
different direction.** [37314354](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37314354/)
(*NEJM*) gives base-edited allogeneic CAR7 T cells for relapsed T-cell ALL — off
the B-cell lineage and off autologous manufacturing in a single trial.
[37648862](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37648862/) (*Nature*) edits the epitope
out of a surface antigen on healthy haematopoietic cells so that a CAR can be
aimed at it on leukaemia, and an independent group publishes the same shielding
logic on CD45 in the same month
[37651540](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37651540/) (*Sci Transl Med*), with
pooled knock-in screening [37714135](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37714135/)
(*Cell*) making such designs searchable rather than hand-built.
[36658341](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36658341/) (*Nat Biotechnol*) points
chimeric autoantibody receptor T cells at the autoantigen-specific B cells of
myasthenia gravis — off oncology entirely. Manufacturing, antigen space and
indication all moved in four weeks.

**Three groups, one ligand family, on `next-gen-checkpoints`.**
[37460871](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37460871/) (*Nat Cancer*) nominates
Siglec-9 as a macrophage checkpoint restricting T-cell priming in glioblastoma;
[37709296](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37709296/) (*JITC*) nominates Siglec-9
macrophages as an immunosuppressive subset with therapeutic vulnerability in
ovarian cancer in the same month; and
[37467314](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37467314/) (*Sci Transl Med*) targeted
the Siglec–sialic acid axis in glioblastoma two months ago. The thread's recorded
pattern is that surface receptor nominations have a half-life of a few months and
ligand-side ones last longer. This is a ligand-side nomination arriving from
three directions at once.

**Two proteome-wide variant-effect models within weeks, each flagged by its own
journal.** [37563329](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37563329/) (*Nat Genet*,
News & Views [37563330](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37563330/)) scores
disease variant effects genome-wide from a protein language model;
[37733863](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37733863/) (*Science*, perspective
[37725046](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37725046/)) does proteome-wide
missense prediction. Two labs reaching clinical variant interpretation from
self-supervised sequence models at the same time, and both editorial boards
thought it worth annotating. Separately
[37592105](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37592105/) (*Nat Med*) builds a
vision–language model for pathology out of scraped public images and presents it
in a clinical journal as a foundation model.

**Three screening-effectiveness readouts in one month.**
[37478397](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37478397/) (*JCO*) compares two
blood-based approaches to nasopharyngeal carcinoma screening head to head on
performance and operational feasibility;
[37667043](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37667043/) (*Nat Cancer*) reports a
prospective multicentre hepatocellular carcinoma screening cohort; and
[37379494](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37379494/) (*JCO*) reports a mortality
benefit for a blood biomarker panel in the PLCO cohort. `interception` also gains
a model that predicts myeloid neoplasia risk before the disease exists
[37620601](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37620601/) (*Nat Genet*).

**What is absent, having looked.** Across the 2,855 titles of this quarter there
is not one paper describing an LLM agent that plans, calls tools or acts. The
nearest items are answerers: a chat model benchmarked on biomedical text
generation and mining [37682111](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37682111/)
(*Bioinformatics*), and a clinical-journal pair reporting that large language
models answer medical questions accurately without matching clinicians' knowledge
[37548971](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37548971/) and asking how such models
should be built and adopted
[37548965](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37548965/). `agentic-ai` holds one
earlier card in this corpus, a commentary on a chatbot rather than an agent
[36988602](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36988602/), and the months between
that and this one are empty. This matters more than a positive would: eleven of
the thirteen threads open in January 2023, the month the window itself opens,
which is a fact about where reading started rather than about the world.
`agentic-ai` does not, and its silence here was measured rather than assumed. `clinical-practice` is empty too, for a duller reason — a title cannot
say a result was presented at a meeting, so the thread is untestable against a
title-only index, and it was left alone rather than padded.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Four of the month's refutations land on cell populations that had been nominated
for removal.

[37713507](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37713507/) (*Sci Immunol*) — lung
tumour-infiltrating regulatory T cells split into transcriptionally and
functionally divergent subsets that track differently with checkpoint blockade
response, with [37713508](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37713508/) mapping the
network that makes some of them suppressive and
[37563309](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37563309/) (*Nat Immunol*) finding the
same divergence in resident macrophages. Depleting Tregs as a population removes
both arms of something that has two.

[37525015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37525015/) (*Nat Cancer*, with
[37553501](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37553501/)) — IL-17 signalling,
routinely nominated as tumour-promoting, is associated with clinical benefit from
combined CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade in patients. Uncarded but pointing the same
way, [37572655](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37572655/) (*Immunity*) has
CTLA-4 blockade recruiting microglia — a population nominated for depletion in
glioblastoma — into the effector arm.

[37537301](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37537301/) (*Nat Cancer*) — CD8 T cells
keep killing MHC-I-negative tumour cells through NKG2D and its ligands. Loss of
antigen presentation is scored as an escape route throughout this literature;
here it is not sufficient on its own.

[37653344](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37653344/) (*Nat Med*) — myeloma
escapes both BCMA- and GPRC5D-directed immunotherapy through defined antigen-loss
mechanisms. Each new target inherits the failure mode, which is the argument
against reading the platform's reach as a function of how many antigens can be
found. Section 3's three supporting cards and this one are the same thread in the
same month, and both readings are correct.

### (b) Method credibility

Three cards, and one of them lands on a second thread.

[37723583](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37723583/) (*Genome Biol*) — methods
for calling spatially variable genes disagree with each other, reported as the
reason to benchmark them. It refutes `single-cell-3d-genome` as well, which is
why that thread reads +1 / −1: the claim is that spatial multi-omics becomes a
routine modality that downstream pipelines ingest, and the pipelines do not yet
agree on what they are reading.

[37734322](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37734322/) (*Cell Systems*) — the
two-dimensional embeddings that single-cell papers are read from misrepresent the
data they display. The figure and the finding are in different places.

[37669666](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37669666/) (*Cell*) is a retraction
notice; [37616332](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37616332/) (*Science*) and
[37548412](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37548412/) (*NAR*) are editorial
expressions of concern in the same four weeks, and
[37717594](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37717594/) (*Lancet*) reports an
institution halting projects over a fraud investigation. As every month, this
thread can only refute, so +0 / −22 cumulative describes the instrument and not a
decline. What the quarter does show is where the audit has got to: the clustering
step, the embedding the clusters are viewed in, the spatial caller, and the
correction notice itself.
